validity.recommendation: no change — existence and classification confirmed
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: real, continuously FERC-regulated interstate pipeline. FERC Docket CP04-371-000 (Order, Nov 3, 2004, wayback-verified — the sheet's own cited source, dead at the live FERC URL but recovered via Wayback) states Chandeleur Pipe Line Company 'is an interstate pipeline providing open access transportation service' whose system 'originates in the Outer Continental Shelf, passes through both Louisiana and Mississippi state waters, and terminates onshore near Pascagoula, Mississippi.' Independently confirmed continuously operating across four decades of FERC dockets I located beyond the harvested pool: Docket RP99-329-000 (1999 tariff filing), Docket CP01-81-000 (2001 Federal Register notice, capacity increase 280,000->321,000 Mcf/d), Docket CP04-48-002 (2009 notice, MAGS gathering-interest acquisition), and a Dec 1, 2025 FERC compliance filing (Docket RP26-258-000, 'Chandeleur LAUF Filing') naming 'Chandeleur Pipe Line, LLC' as an active tariff filer — this is 3 weeks before this sweep. Correctly classified as a transmission trunk (not gathering/gathering-only); its 2004-2009 acquisition of an interest in the offshore Mobile Area Gathering System (MAGS) added gathering-line interest but did not reclassify the certificated transmission line. DUPLICATE CHECK: compared against all 49 other rows in the 50-pipeline Gulf Coast roster — no physical-pipe overlap found; Chandeleur is the only OCS-to-Pascagoula line in the set (Destin, Garden Banks, Independence Trail, Mississippi Canyon, Nautilus, Sea Robin are separate, geographically distinct OCS lines with different landfalls/blocks). Harvested wiki citation pool for this row: 5 citations. Opened/attempted 4 of 5 (abarrelfull.wikidot.com skipped per the standing ban); FERC C-2.pdf and the EnLink press release recovered live via Wayback (both dead at their original URLs); the 1997 PR Newswire 'Chevron's Chandeleur Pipe Line to Expand' (thefreelibrary.com) is 403-blocked with NO Wayback capture available (checked the CDX API) — could not read it, flagging as unreadable rather than treating the 403 as a deletion; the 1995 DOI OCS lease-sale EIS on Google Books returned 200 but the 'Chandeleur' substring did not surface in the scanned preview text — not used. All value/spec findings from the additional, non-harvested sources I found are filed separately below (attribution + spec concerns) and in fills[].

validity.recommendation: update Owner1 from 'EnLink Midstream' to 'Third Coast Midstream, LLC' — ownership changed 2019-10-31, six years before this sweep
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's current Owner1 = 'EnLink Midstream' (100%) is STALE. A PHMSA enforcement Warning Letter (CPF 4-2020-003-WL, Oct 2, 2020, addressed to Third Coast Midstream LLC's VP of Operations) states in an official finding: 'Third Coast Midstream obtained the Chandeleur Pipeline from Enlink Processing Services on October 31, 2019. Notice to PHMSA's National Registry was not provided until May 22, 2020, 144 days beyond the required 60 day notification period.' This is a primary federal regulatory record, independent of both companies. A second, independent source — Rextag Corporation's current (accessed 2026-09-04) informational-postings page for 'Chandeleur Pipe Line' — states 'Owner: Third Coast Midstream, LLC / Operator: Chandeleur Pipe Line Company', corroborating the same current owner. I also checked whether a further, more recent sale moved Chandeleur again: Basalt Infrastructure's 'Black Bear Transmission' portfolio company acquired a bundle of Third Coast Midstream gas-transmission assets in 2019-2020, but that bundle is described (BusinessWire, 2020-06-29/09-09) as 'six INTRASTATE natural gas pipelines...in Alabama, Louisiana and Mississippi' — Chandeleur is INTERSTATE (FERC NGA-jurisdictional, confirmed above), so it does not appear to be part of that divestiture; the Dec 2025 FERC filer name 'Chandeleur Pipe Line, LLC' is consistent with continued Third Coast Midstream ownership, not a further sale. Proposed correction staged in fills[] below (Owner unit) rather than applied — per hard requirement, no live-sheet write without explicit per-batch authorization.

validity.recommendation: flag for Baird adjudication — do not silently change LengthKnown; the 346 km value is well-sourced but a current independent source states a much shorter figure for what may be a narrower entity scope
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's LengthKnown = 346.00 km (215 mi) matches EnLink Midstream's own 2014 acquisition disclosure almost to the decimal ('Chandeleur System: ~215 miles of offshore Mississippi and Alabama pipelines' — 215 mi x 1.60934 = 346.0 km exactly; wayback-verified EnLink press release, reprinted near-verbatim by Oil & Gas Journal so I do not count OGJ as a second independent origin for this figure). However, Rextag Corporation's CURRENT (2026-09-04) informational-postings page for the FERC-regulated entity states 'Miles of Pipeline: 68' for 'Chandeleur Pipe Line' — a >3x disagreement with the sheet value and with EnLink's own figure. My read: EnLink's 215-mile 'Chandeleur System' figure is likely a broader asset bundle (including the offshore Mobile Area Gathering System interest Chandeleur acquired 2004-2009, per FERC Docket CP04-48-002) while Rextag's 68-mile figure may report only the core FERC-certificated 'Chandeleur Pipe Line' mainline (Order 636 informational-postings scope). I could not independently confirm which figure GEM's single P0165 row is meant to represent (the row carries no segment_name to disambiguate), and I found no third source stating an exact mileage. Filing as a spec concern rather than silently keeping or changing the value — Baird should decide whether the row should carry the system total (346 km, current value, kept in fills[] as REFS_ADDED) or be split/re-scoped to the certificated mainline only.
